note: The journal's ground pages, what a tap on the ground says, and the almanac (docs 13, 15). groundOrder: the ground pages, in order. Each ground: name, icon, measure (share: of the open dry land; area: square meters), amount ([at least, words] steps, as for plants), field (field notes learned by triggers: seen, moment:<id>), fieldHint, and tap (the noun a tap uses). moss: ground counts as mossy where moisture is at least mossMoisture and salt under mossSalt (0..1), on land that is not standing water, as the live moss grows. wet and salt: words for a tapped spot by its moisture and salt (0..1), the first step it reaches from the top. depth: words for a tapped water's depth in meters ([under, words]). suits: plants you know with suitability at least suitAt are named on the card; unknown: the pencil line when a species you have not met would like it. almanac: words for the almanac page: parts of the day by hour ([from hour, words]); moods; wind by strength ([at least, words]); the moon by phase (0 new, 0.5 full; [under, words]); daylight by day length in hours; tide words; hourWords to say a few hours in words.

soil.name: Soil
amount: Hardly any bare soil shows on the island.
Bare soil shows here and there.
Much of the island is bare soil.

field.text: Soil holds water and food for roots; most plants start here.
After rain the soil darkens and smells sweet.
Morning mist settles low over damp soil and lifts as the sun warms it.

soil.fieldHint: Watch the ground in other weather to learn more.

sand.name: Sand
amount: Hardly any sand on the island.
Sand rings the shore.
Sand covers much of the island.

field.text: Sand drains fast, so little can hold on to it except where the sea keeps it wet.
Wet sand darkens and firms; you could almost walk on it like a road.
At dawn the low sun picks out every ripple the wind left in it.

sand.fieldHint: Watch the shore in other light and weather to learn more.

rock.name: Rock
amount: Hardly any rock shows on the island.
Rock breaks through in places.
Rock covers much of the island.

field.text: Rock sheds water quickly; only moss finds a hold on it, and only where it stays damp.
Wet rock glistens, and the moss on it greens up within hours.
Rock warms slowly and cools slowly: on a winter morning it is the last place the frost leaves.

rock.fieldHint: Watch the rocks in other weather to learn more.

moss.name: Moss
amount: No moss grows on the island yet.
A little moss grows on the damp ground.
Moss carpets the damp banks.
Moss covers much of the damp ground.

field.text: Moss has no roots; it drinks through its leaves wherever the ground stays damp.
After rain it swells and brightens in a few hours.
In mist it holds the droplets like a sponge.

moss.fieldHint: Watch the moss in other weather to learn more.

fresh.name: Fresh water
amount: No fresh water stands on the island.
A small pool of fresh water.
A pond of fresh water.
A large pond of fresh water.
fresh.stream: A stream runs from it to the sea.

field.text: Still water warms quickly in the sun and fills with tiny life that others feed on.
Rain rings the pond's surface and slowly raises it.
Mist forms first over still water on calm, cool mornings.

fresh.fieldHint: Watch the water in other weather to learn more.

shore.name: Shore and sea
amount: The sea comes right up to the land.
A narrow tide band rings the island.
A wide tide band rings the island.

field.text: Twice a day the tide covers the band, and twice a day it leaves it bare.
Only plants that can bear salt grow in the spray above it.
In winter the sea runs grey and the band stays wet longer.

shore.fieldHint: Watch the shore at other times to learn more.

water.sea: The open sea, deep and salty.
water.band: The tide band: wet twice a day when the sea comes in.

suitsNone: Nothing you know would grow here.
unknown: Something you have not met might like it here.
